thought.text: I see! Port 8080 is **code-server** (VSCode), NOT the game! Let me find the game port:

reasoning_content:
The PM2 areloria is the game server. Port 8080 is code-server (VS Code), which is not what we want on the main domain. Let me check what's listening on port 8080:- Process 760 = code-server (VSCode running on port 8080)

So we have two Node processes:1. PM2 areloria (pid 3159501) - runs the game server, but on what port?
2. Process 760 = code-server (VSCode) - on port 8080 (which shouldn't be there)

Let me check what the game server (PM2) is listening on. PM2 says it's online with uptime 15m but we don't see what port. Let me check for any Node processes on ports.

action.command:
cd /workspace/project && python3 << 'EOF'
import paramiko
client = paramiko.SSHClient()
client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
client.connect("46.202.154.25", 22, "root", "2N00py123+++")

# Check PM2 process port
stdin, stdout, stderr = client.exec_command("cat /root/.pm2/pids/areloria-0.pid 2>&1")
pid = stdout.read().decode().strip()
print("Game PID:", pid)

# Check what port that process uses
stdin, stdout, stderr = client.exec_command(f"netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep {pid} || ss -tlnp | grep {pid}")
print("Ports:", stdout.read().decode())

# Check all node processes
stdin, stdout, stderr = client.exec_command("ps aux | grep 'node.*index.js' | grep -v grep")
print("\nNode games:", stdout.read().decode())

client.close()
EOF
